title: the DSG hireling loyalty and hazards

banner.title: The DSG HIRELING LOYALTY AND THE P. 55 HAZARDS, R524: printed pp. 54-55 (pdf 55-56) - the hireling loyalty: a PC group cannot usually run a mine alone (even with a miner-proficiency supervisor, a large mine needs hired strong arms; adventurers better used as scouts and guards when the claim is questionable or monsters possible), loyalty insignificant in iron or copper mines but a precious-metal or gemstone find a great temptation, the standard DMG page-36 Loyalty Check with the foreman as the liege, the + or - 10% security modifiers (a post-shift search +10%, no PCs present at shift end -10%), pay evaluated against the mine's value (the 1,000 gp of diamonds for a 20 gp wage), and the failed check not an immediate grab-and-run - the DM weighs the NPC's Intelligence, only perhaps 8-or-less attempting unplanned theft, exceptionally high Intelligence preparing the theft and the getaway or concealment, the thief stealing 1d6 x 10% of his daily output; the natural hazards: flooding from a tapped underground water body or digging below the water table (adjudicated from the DM's map, the below-level escape very difficult, at-level a race to the exit, above-level easy; the flooded mine needing draining or pumping), and mine cave-ins (shoring partially preventing but never eliminating - a tunnel shored every 10 feet at 2% weekly, no shoring 50%, partial shoring interpolated; external forces adding an earthquake 1d4 x 10%, a heavy rain or flood 1d3 x 10%, burrowers like umber hulks and ankhegs 1% per hit die; the d100 location roll from one designated end 01 to the other 100; the automatic 20-foot-long, 10-foot-thick fallen ceiling; chain reactions checked normally); and the unnatural hazards: the unnamed evil lurking deep in the earth at DM creativity (the burial-ground undead, the concerned deep monsters), the drow and duergar regarding mineral wealth as their own with intervention rising in direct proportion to the mine's value, and the planar-gate risk - the vigorous miners breaking through to another plane, or much more likely some horrid lower-plane denizen finding a path into the world up the deep-plunging tunnel
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~7048-7215) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 127 = the printed p. 54 window, idx 129 = the printed p. 55 window); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the 10% modifiers, the Intelligence-8 threshold, the 1d6 x 10% theft, the 2%/50% shored/unshored weekly cave-in chances, the 1d4 x 10% earthquake and 1d3 x 10% rain adds, the 1% per hit die, the d100 location roll, the 20 x 10 ft ceiling, and the 1200-ft/30-roll/360-ft worked example. SEAMS: the DMG page-36 Loyalty Check (cross-book, nothing auto-credited), the R520 shoring rules (the every-10-foot interval matching the R520 per-10-foot-section braces), the R511 chain-reaction cave-in rules, the R518 water-travel rules, and the R503 hazards survey. The mining block is fully closed with this round (all children 118-133 flipped); the natural/unnatural hazards are the last open children of the big underground-environment chapter (pp. 36-55), so the chapter parent line becomes closeable at the next census check. The new-equipment chapter (Table 35) starts the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: A prose round: no tables pin. The dice pin as consts per the R508 convention - the 1d6 x 10% theft of daily output, the 1d4 x 10% earthquake and 1d3 x 10% rain cave-in adds, and the d100 end-to-end cave-in location roll. The thresholds pin as consts: the 10% loyalty modifiers, the Intelligence-8 unplanned-theft line, the 2%/50% shored/unshored weekly chances, the 1% per hit die of burrowers, and the 20 x 10 ft fallen ceiling. The rest pins as prose bools: the hired-help and scout/guard split, the temptation and pay-evaluation rules, the foreman-as-liege check, the Intelligence-driven theft planning, the flooding adjudication and escape gradient, the shoring interpolation, the chain-reaction reference, and the unnamed-evil, burial-ground, deep-monster, jealous-race and planar-gate threats. The DMG-36, R520, R511 and R518 seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnswLoyaltyModPct
consts.comment: the mine-security loyalty modifiers are + or - 10% (a post-shift search +10%, no PCs present at the shift end -10%).

consts.name: dnswTheftDice
consts.comment: the thief-output roll is one die.

consts.name: dnswTheftSides
consts.comment: the thief steals 1d6 x 10% of his daily output.

consts.name: dnswTheftPctMult
consts.comment: the 1d6 result times 10 is the percent of daily output stolen.

consts.name: dnswLowIntUnplanned
consts.comment: only workers with low Intelligence, perhaps 8 or less, attempt a theft with no planning.

consts.name: dnswShoredCaveInPct
consts.comment: a tunnel shored at every 10-foot interval stands only a 2% chance per week of a cave-in (the R520 shoring seam).

consts.name: dnswUnshoredCaveInPct
consts.comment: a tunnel with no shoring whatsoever runs a 50% weekly chance of a cave-in.

consts.name: dnswQuakeDice
consts.comment: the earthquake modifier roll is one die.

consts.name: dnswQuakeSides
consts.comment: an earthquake adds 1d4 x 10% to the cave-in chance.

consts.name: dnswQuakePctMult
consts.comment: the 1d4 result times 10 is the earthquake percent add.

consts.name: dnswRainDice
consts.comment: the heavy-rain modifier roll is one die.

consts.name: dnswRainSides
consts.comment: a heavy rain or flood increases the cave-in chance by 1d3 x 10%.

consts.name: dnswRainPctMult
consts.comment: the 1d3 result times 10 is the rain percent add.

consts.name: dnswBurrowerPctPerHitDie
consts.comment: burrowing creatures such as umber hulks and ankhegs increase the cave-in chance by 1% per hit die of intruding monsters.

consts.name: dnswCaveInLocDice
consts.comment: the cave-in location roll is one die.

consts.name: dnswCaveInLocSides
consts.comment: the DM designates one end of the mine 01 and the other 100 and rolls d100: the result places the cave-in along the tunnel (a 30 on a 1200-foot shaft is about 360 feet from the entrance).

consts.name: dnswCaveInLenFt
consts.comment: a cave-in automatically brings down a ceiling section 20 feet long.

consts.name: dnswCaveInThickFt
consts.comment: the fallen ceiling section is 10 feet thick.

bools.name: dnswHiredHelpRequired
bools.comment: a PC group cannot usually run a mining operation by themselves - even with a miner-proficiency supervisor, a large mine requires hired strong arms.

bools.name: dnswAdventurersScoutAndGuard
bools.comment: if the claim is of questionable legality or a monster attack is possible, skilled adventurers are better used as scouts and guards while low-level laborers excavate.

bools.name: dnswPreciousFindsTempt
bools.comment: hireling loyalty is not a significant problem in an iron or copper mine, but a precious metal or gemstone find presents employees a great opportunity to steal.

bools.name: dnswDmg36LoyaltyCheck
bools.comment: the NPC reaction to temptation uses the standard Loyalty Check procedure outlined in the DMG on page 36 (the cross-book seam).

bools.name: dnswForemanIsLiege
bools.comment: for this Loyalty Check, treat the foreman of the mining operation as the liege when determining modifiers.

bools.name: dnswSecurityModifiers
bools.comment: additional + or - 10% modifiers reflect the mine's security: a post-shift search deters theft (+10%), while no PCs present as the miners leave invites it (-10%).

bools.name: dnswPayJudgedAgainstMineValue
bools.comment: for loyalty modification, the NPC's pay is evaluated against the value of the mine - a miner excavating 1,000 gp of diamonds for 20 gp feels underpaid however good the wage.

bools.name: dnswFailedCheckNotImmediate
bools.comment: a failed Loyalty Check does not mean the NPC immediately pockets valuables and runs - the DM must consider the NPC's Intelligence and concoct a suitable theft plan.

bools.name: dnswHighIntPlansTheft
bools.comment: an exceptionally high Intelligence thief goes to great lengths preparing the theft and ensuring the getaway or concealing that the theft occurred.

bools.name: dnswFloodFromTappedWater
bools.comment: flooding occurs if excavators accidentally tap an underground body of water or dig below the water table; the chance depends on the proximity of such bodies, adjudicated from a carefully drawn DM map.

bools.name: dnswFloodEscapeGradient
bools.comment: characters below the water level have a very difficult time escaping, characters at the flow level race the water to the nearest exit, and characters above escape with relative ease.

bools.name: dnswFloodedMineNeedsPumping
bools.comment: after a flood disaster a mine is very difficult to work unless the water can be drained or pumped away; a mine reaching the water table slowly fills and closes unless water is removed faster than it flows in.

bools.name: dnswShoringPartialNotTotal
bools.comment: proper shoring partially prevents but cannot eliminate cave-ins; a partially shored tunnel's chance is calculated by the DM between the 2% and 50% extremes.

bools.name: dnswExternalForcesAdd
bools.comment: external forces add to the cave-in chance: an earthquake 1d4 x 10%, a heavy rain or flood 1d3 x 10%, and burrowing creatures 1% per hit die.

bools.name: dnswChainReactionNormal
bools.comment: chain reaction cave-ins are checked for normally (the R511 seam).

bools.name: dnswUnnamedEvilLurks
bools.comment: a common element of Underdark campaigns is the unnamed evil lurking deep within the earth - the exact encounter is the DM's creativity, with many things possible where magic is common.

bools.name: dnswBurialGroundUndead
bools.comment: the excavation might penetrate a long-forgotten burial ground, awakening its hideous undead denizens.

bools.name: dnswDeepMonstersConcerned
bools.comment: deep-dwelling monsters may become concerned about surface dwellers penetrating so far under the earth.

bools.name: dnswUnderdarkRacesJealous
bools.comment: Underdark races such as the drow and the duergar regard mineral wealth as their own and look jealously on outsiders exploiting it - the intervention threat rises in direct proportion to the mine's value.

bools.name: dnswPlanarGateRisk
bools.comment: vigorous mining might discover a gate to another plane: miners might pass through inadvertently, or - much more likely - some horrid lower-plane denizen finds a path into the world up the deep-plunging tunnel.

examples.expr: m['dnswLoyaltyModPct']() != 10 or m['dnswTheftDice']() != 1 or m['dnswTheftSides']() != 6 or m['dnswTheftPctMult']() != 10 or m['dnswLowIntUnplanned']() != 8

examples.note: the cave-in chances: 2% shored vs 50% unshored weekly, the 1d4 x 10% earthquake and 1d3 x 10% rain adds, and the 1% per hit die of burrowers.

examples.expr: m['dnswCaveInLocDice']() != 1 or m['dnswCaveInLocSides']() != 100 or m['dnswCaveInLenFt']() != 20 or m['dnswCaveInThickFt']() != 10
examples.note: the cave-in geometry: the d100 end-to-end location roll and the 20-foot-long, 10-foot-thick fallen ceiling section.

examples.expr: m['dnswDmg36LoyaltyCheck']() != 1 or m['dnswForemanIsLiege']() != 1 or m['dnswFailedCheckNotImmediate']() != 1 or m['dnswHighIntPlansTheft']() != 1 or m['dnswFloodFromTappedWater']() != 1 or m['dnswShoringPartialNotTotal']() != 1 or m['dnswUnderdarkRacesJealous']() != 1 or m['dnswPlanarGateRisk']() != 1
